title: EDAC Memory Error Tracking
exclusions: Monitors Linux memory-controller error counters exposed under `/sys/devices/system/edac/mc/mc*` by a loaded EDAC driver. It does not prove that installed memory has ECC capability, that firmware enabled correction, that every memory controller is supported, or that EDAC owns errors reported through APEI/GHES, MCA/MCE, CXL, a hypervisor, guest virtual hardware, a BMC, or vendor firmware. A corrected error means the reporting mechanism corrected that occurrence; it does not mean the DIMM is healthy or predict a later uncorrected error with certainty. An EDAC UE is uncorrected (the sysfs ABI also calls `ue_count` uncorrectable), but it is not necessarily fatal; conversely, `panic_on_ue` can stop the host before the sysfs UE counter increments. Controller totals and per-DIMM totals are related views and must not be added together. The search detects positive cumulative-counter deltas, not lifetime nonzero values, raw log-line counts, physical slot identity, data corruption, or root cause. It excludes first observations, malformed/duplicate minute buckets, stale samples, unsupported/missing sysfs trees, and notification-only exceptions for corrected errors. Kernel/rasdaemon events and missing-source monitoring remain separate corroborating controls. This operational use case is not regulatory attestation.
evidence: When deployed, retain the Linux kernel and EDAC driver versions, ECC/firmware inventory, `find /sys/devices/system/edac/mc -maxdepth 2 -type f` inventory or equivalent reviewed manifest, controller names, DIMM labels/locations, effective `panic_on_ue` and EDAC log settings, the version-controlled `TA_linux_edac` collector and Splunk input/parsing configuration, and the `linux_edac_memory_error_tracking` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, and triggered rows. Alert exports should preserve `_time`, `host`, `boot_id`, `mc`, `mc_name`, `severity`, `alert_reason`, corrected and uncorrected controller deltas, unattributed deltas, changed-DIMM context, reset/wrap flag, and `seconds_since_reset`. Retain the matching raw sysfs snapshots, contemporaneous kernel journal and rasdaemon/ras-mc-ctl output when available, ticket disposition, and positive/negative fixture results. These artifacts show what the documented Linux and Splunk paths observed; they do not prove that no memory error occurred outside those paths.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index, emit schema-valid `source=linux_edac_sysfs sourcetype=linux:edac:sysfs` JSON rows for `host=uc-edac-102`, one fixed `boot_id`, `mc=mc0`, and both `scope=controller,entity=mc0` and `scope=dimm,entity=dimm0` once per minute. Put a baseline immediately before the five-minute alert window with controller CE/UE totals 20/0, no-information totals 2/0, DIMM totals 18/0, and `seconds_since_reset=600`. In the first alert-window minute raise controller CE to 23 and DIMM CE to 21 while seconds increases; keep subsequent samples stable. Expect exactly one WARNING result with `controller_ce_delta=3`, `controller_ue_delta=0`, `ce_noinfo_delta=0`, and `changed_dimms` naming dimm0. In a separate run, raise controller and DIMM UE from 0 to 1; expect exactly one CRITICAL `uncorrected_error` result. Confirm that controller totals, not controller plus DIMM totals, drive the reported deltas.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run isolated variants with the same field contract. Keep all cumulative counters unchanged across a valid baseline and five alert-window samples and expect zero rows. Start with nonzero lifetime totals but no prior sample and expect zero rows because the first observation is a baseline. Decrease counters to zero while `seconds_since_reset` also decreases and expect zero rows with no negative or lifetime-sized delta; then set the post-reset CE count to 2 and confirm one warning carrying `counter_boundary_detected=1` and a lower-bound delta of 2. In separate runs, duplicate one host/controller/scope/entity minute, omit `boot_id`, use `collector_status=error`, make a counter negative, or place the newest sample outside the freshness window; each must produce no alert row and must be caught by source-health review. Finally, apply an exact active exception to a corrected-only fixture and confirm notification suppression, then verify the same exception cannot suppress an uncorrected-error result.

dataSources: Primary signal: one-line JSON snapshots every 60 seconds from a customer-managed Splunk Universal Forwarder scripted input reading `/sys/devices/system/edac/mc/mc*/{ce_count,ue_count,ce_noinfo_count,ue_noinfo_count,seconds_since_reset,mc_name}` and, when present, `(dimm|rank)*/{dimm_ce_count,dimm_ue_count,dimm_label,dimm_location}`. Route them to the deployment-local `index=os`, `source=linux_edac_sysfs`, and `sourcetype=linux:edac:sysfs`. Required event fields are `event_version`, `collector`, `collector_status`, `observed_at_epoch`, `boot_id`, `mc`, `scope`, `entity`, `mc_name`, `seconds_since_reset`, `ce_count`, and `ue_count`; controller rows also require both no-information counters. Kernel journal/syslog EDAC messages and rasdaemon trace-event/SQLite records are independent corroboration and cover event detail or panic paths that periodic sysfs polling can miss; they are not mixed into the primary cumulative-delta SPL.
app: A customer-managed `TA_linux_edac` app containing the local Python scripted input and `linux:edac:sysfs` parsing configuration, plus a search app containing the saved search, dashboard, and `edac_memory_exceptions.csv`. No premium Splunk app or Splunkbase add-on is required. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux can collect adjacent kernel/journal context, but it does not provide this EDAC sysfs snapshot contract.
spl:
index=os source=linux_edac_sysfs sourcetype=linux:edac:sysfs collector=linux_edac_sysfs_v1 collector_status=ok earliest=-12m@m latest=-2m@m
| eval event_version=tonumber(event_version), observed_at_epoch=tonumber(observed_at_epoch), seconds_since_reset=tonumber(seconds_since_reset), ce_count=tonumber(ce_count), ue_count=tonumber(ue_count), ce_noinfo_count=tonumber(ce_noinfo_count), ue_noinfo_count=tonumber(ue_noinfo_count)
| where event_version=1 AND isnotnull(host) AND match(boot_id,"^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$") AND match(mc,"^mc[0-9]+$") AND in(scope,"controller","dimm") AND len(entity)>0 AND observed_at_epoch>0 AND seconds_since_reset>=0 AND ce_count>=0 AND ue_count>=0 AND (scope="dimm" OR (ce_noinfo_count>=0 AND ue_noinfo_count>=0))
| eval ce_noinfo_count=if(scope="controller",ce_noinfo_count,0), ue_noinfo_count=if(scope="controller",ue_noinfo_count,0), _time=observed_at_epoch
| bin _time span=1m
| stats count as bucket_samples latest(mc_name) as mc_name latest(dimm_label) as dimm_label latest(dimm_location) as dimm_location latest(seconds_since_reset) as seconds_since_reset latest(ce_count) as ce_count latest(ue_count) as ue_count latest(ce_noinfo_count) as ce_noinfo_count latest(ue_noinfo_count) as ue_noinfo_count by _time host boot_id mc scope entity
| where bucket_samples=1
| sort 0 host boot_id mc scope entity _time
| streamstats current=f window=1 last(seconds_since_reset) as previous_seconds_since_reset last(ce_count) as previous_ce_count last(ue_count) as previous_ue_count last(ce_noinfo_count) as previous_ce_noinfo_count last(ue_noinfo_count) as previous_ue_noinfo_count by host boot_id mc scope entity
| eval timer_reset=if(isnotnull(previous_seconds_since_reset) AND seconds_since_reset<previous_seconds_since_reset,1,0), ce_boundary=if(timer_reset=1 OR (isnotnull(previous_ce_count) AND ce_count<previous_ce_count),1,0), ue_boundary=if(timer_reset=1 OR (isnotnull(previous_ue_count) AND ue_count<previous_ue_count),1,0), ce_noinfo_boundary=if(timer_reset=1 OR (isnotnull(previous_ce_noinfo_count) AND ce_noinfo_count<previous_ce_noinfo_count),1,0), ue_noinfo_boundary=if(timer_reset=1 OR (isnotnull(previous_ue_noinfo_count) AND ue_noinfo_count<previous_ue_noinfo_count),1,0)
| eval ce_delta=case(isnull(previous_ce_count),0,ce_boundary=1,ce_count,true(),ce_count-previous_ce_count), ue_delta=case(isnull(previous_ue_count),0,ue_boundary=1,ue_count,true(),ue_count-previous_ue_count), ce_noinfo_delta=case(isnull(previous_ce_noinfo_count),0,ce_noinfo_boundary=1,ce_noinfo_count,true(),ce_noinfo_count-previous_ce_noinfo_count), ue_noinfo_delta=case(isnull(previous_ue_noinfo_count),0,ue_noinfo_boundary=1,ue_noinfo_count,true(),ue_noinfo_count-previous_ue_noinfo_count), counter_boundary=if(ce_boundary=1 OR ue_boundary=1 OR ce_noinfo_boundary=1 OR ue_noinfo_boundary=1,1,0)
| eval in_alert_window=if(_time>=relative_time(now(),"-7m@m") AND _time<relative_time(now(),"-2m@m"),1,0), controller_ce_delta=if(scope="controller" AND in_alert_window=1,ce_delta,0), controller_ue_delta=if(scope="controller" AND in_alert_window=1,ue_delta,0), controller_ce_noinfo_delta=if(scope="controller" AND in_alert_window=1,ce_noinfo_delta,0), controller_ue_noinfo_delta=if(scope="controller" AND in_alert_window=1,ue_noinfo_delta,0), controller_boundary=if(scope="controller" AND in_alert_window=1,counter_boundary,0), controller_sample_time=if(scope="controller",_time,null()), controller_seconds_since_reset=if(scope="controller",seconds_since_reset,null())
| eval changed_dimm=if(scope="dimm" AND in_alert_window=1 AND (ce_delta>0 OR ue_delta>0),entity . ":" . coalesce(dimm_label,"unlabelled") . ":" . coalesce(dimm_location,"location-unavailable") . ":CE+" . tostring(ce_delta) . ":UE+" . tostring(ue_delta),null())
| stats max(controller_sample_time) as _time latest(mc_name) as mc_name latest(controller_seconds_since_reset) as seconds_since_reset sum(controller_ce_delta) as controller_ce_delta sum(controller_ue_delta) as controller_ue_delta sum(controller_ce_noinfo_delta) as ce_noinfo_delta sum(controller_ue_noinfo_delta) as ue_noinfo_delta max(controller_boundary) as counter_boundary_detected values(changed_dimm) as changed_dimms by host boot_id mc
| where _time>=relative_time(now(),"-4m@m") AND (controller_ce_delta>0 OR controller_ue_delta>0)
| eval severity=if(controller_ue_delta>0,"critical","warning"), alert_reason=case(controller_ue_delta>0 AND controller_ce_delta>0,"uncorrected_and_corrected_errors",controller_ue_delta>0,"uncorrected_error",true(),"corrected_error"), use_case="UC-1.1.102"
| lookup edac_memory_exceptions.csv host mc use_case OUTPUT valid_from_epoch valid_until_epoch exception_reason exception_owner exception_ticket
| eval exception_active=if(isnotnull(valid_from_epoch) AND isnotnull(valid_until_epoch) AND tonumber(valid_from_epoch)<=now() AND now()<tonumber(valid_until_epoch),1,0)
| where controller_ue_delta>0 OR exception_active=0
| table _time host boot_id mc mc_name severity alert_reason controller_ce_delta controller_ue_delta ce_noinfo_delta ue_noinfo_delta changed_dimms counter_boundary_detected seconds_since_reset exception_reason exception_owner exception_ticket
| sort 0 -severity -controller_ue_delta -controller_ce_delta host mc
description: Detects new Linux EDAC memory errors by differencing consecutive per-controller sysfs snapshots within a fixed five-minute alert window. It reports any positive corrected-error delta as a warning and any positive uncorrected-error delta as critical, handles reboot/reset/wrap boundaries without creating negative or lifetime-sized spikes, preserves unattributed-error counts, and adds per-DIMM changes only as localization context rather than double-counting them.
value: Corrected memory errors can be an early maintenance signal while uncorrected errors can precede or accompany application failure, host isolation, data loss, or a kernel panic. Reliable deltas accelerate hardware triage by letting teams distinguish a new occurrence from an old nonzero lifetime counter, identify the affected controller or candidate slot, preserve evidence before reboot or replacement, and escalate the materially different uncorrected path without claiming that every corrected error predicts failure.
implementation: Deploy the supplied read-only EDAC sysfs collector in a managed Universal Forwarder app at a 60-second interval, extract its one-line JSON at search time, and operate a separate freshness/schema check. Save the SPL as `linux_edac_memory_error_tracking`, schedule it every five minutes on minute boundaries with a measured two-minute ingestion delay, and trigger on returned rows. Treat any new corrected count as warning evidence and any new uncorrected count as critical; never add controller and DIMM counters or infer health from a zero/missing counter. Corroborate alerts with kernel journal, rasdaemon, firmware/BMC, physical inventory, and workload impact before hardware action.
visualization: Use a current-alert table with host, controller, controller type, severity, reason, corrected/uncorrected deltas, no-information deltas, changed-DIMM context, reset/wrap flag, seconds since reset, and boot ID. Add separate per-controller time charts for corrected and uncorrected deltas; do not chart cumulative totals as event rates unless the panel explicitly computes reset-aware deltas. Show a controller/DIMM inventory panel with labels and locations, a source-health panel for missing or malformed snapshots, and annotations from kernel/rasdaemon events. Never label corrected errors as harmless, uncorrected errors as invariably fatal, or a DIMM counter plus its controller counter as two errors.
dataModelAcceleration: No standard Splunk Common Information Model dataset preserves Linux EDAC controller identity, boot identity, reset timer, cumulative corrected/uncorrected and no-information counters, or DIMM location. There is no faithful accelerated `tstats` replacement. At large scale, a validated summary index may retain one-minute raw counter snapshots and reset metadata, but the alert must continue to calculate deltas per host, boot, controller, scope, and entity.

knownFalsePositives:
The qualified signal is a real increase in a kernel-maintained counter. A false positive therefore means the increase was expected, misattributed, duplicated by collection, or routed too aggressively; ordinary CPU, package, backup, and monitoring load do not synthetically increment EDAC counters.

1. **Approved error-injection or hardware validation** — EDAC driver injection nodes, firmware diagnostics, vendor burn-in, and laboratory fault injection can deliberately increment CE or UE telemetry. Correlate the exact host, controller, injector, test owner, change ticket, and bounded UTC interval. Never inject an uncorrected error on production hardware merely to test this alert.

2. **Corrected error during a known maintenance observation period** — A hardware team may deliberately observe a low corrected-error rate while arranging replacement. The event remains real. Keep it in evidence, suppress only repeated corrected notifications for the exact host/controller and approved interval, and continue to page on every UE.

3. **Incorrect or missing physical DIMM labels** — EDAC `dimm_label` values are assigned from platform-specific user-space knowledge and can be blank, generic, stale after service, or different from chassis silk-screen labels. Treat `changed_dimms` as a candidate location until reconciled with SMBIOS, BMC/vendor inventory, serial numbers, and the service manual.

4. **Collector duplication or host-identity collision** — Two scripted-input stanzas, a cloned Splunk `host`, or overlapping forwarding paths can produce duplicate minute buckets or merge counters from different machines. The SPL rejects duplicate buckets and partitions by `boot_id`, but source health must identify and repair the collection defect; do not deduplicate unrelated machines into one counter history.

5. **Counter reset, EDAC driver reload, reboot, or wrap** — `reset_counters`, driver initialization, controller rebind, reboot, and a counter-width boundary can make totals decrease. The search uses boot identity and `seconds_since_reset`, records a boundary, and uses the current value as the observable lower-bound increment after that boundary. It cannot recover errors that occurred before a reset and before a successful poll; inspect kernel/rasdaemon records.

6. **Different reporting ownership or granularity** — A firmware-first APEI/GHES path, MCA/MCE decoder, guest, CXL device, or unsupported controller can report errors without populating this sysfs tree, and some drivers cannot localize an event to a DIMM. That is a coverage limitation or no-information alert, not a reason to map arbitrary kernel text to a DIMM.

**Notification suppression mechanism:** preserve raw snapshots and alert history. The CSV lookup edac_memory_exceptions uses headers `host,mc,use_case,valid_from_epoch,valid_until_epoch,exception_reason,exception_owner,exception_ticket`. Require an exact host, exact `mcN`, literal `UC-1.1.102`, numeric bounded UTC epochs, owner, reason, and ticket. Reject wildcards, open-ended or expired rows, and exceptions created only because a counter is noisy. The SPL applies an active exception only to corrected-only notification; any positive uncorrected delta bypasses it.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and semantic boundary

Assign Linux platform, hardware, Splunk collection, and incident-response owners. Use a kernel with the appropriate EDAC memory-controller driver loaded and a host whose firmware and memory configuration actually provide error correction. Confirm the primary tree exists at `/sys/devices/system/edac/mc` and contains one or more `mcN` directories. The forwarder account needs read and directory-traverse access to the documented sysfs attributes and `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`; it needs no write access to `reset_counters`, no root shell, no `sudo`, and no permission to change EDAC logging, panic behavior, firmware, scrubbing, or memory repair. The Splunk search role needs read access to the selected OS index and exception lookup plus permission to schedule the saved search and alert action.

Treat terminology precisely. A corrected error (CE) means the reporting path detected and corrected that occurrence; the machine can continue, but repeated CEs may justify preventive maintenance. It is not proof that the DIMM is healthy, and the kernel documentation says CE harvesting can, but need not, predict a future UE. An uncorrected error (UE) means correction did not succeed. The EDAC sysfs ABI describes `ue_count` as uncorrectable, while the EDAC driver API uses `HW_EVENT_ERR_UNCORRECTED`; neither term alone means the host must have crashed. Some uncorrected errors are recoverable or affect unused memory. If panic-on-UE is enabled, a panic can occur before `ue_count` increments, so absence of a delta cannot prove absence of an event.

Controller `ce_count` and `ue_count` are cumulative totals since driver initialization or the last counter reset. `ce_noinfo_count` and `ue_noinfo_count` are cumulative subsets that could not be attributed to a slot. Per-DIMM `dimm_ce_count` and `dimm_ue_count` localize some of the controller events. They are not independent totals: never add a DIMM delta to the controller delta. `seconds_since_reset` is the reset-age signal supplied specifically to support rate calculations. A first observation is only a baseline; treating a lifetime total as new would create a false incident on every onboarding or search-window boundary.

## Step 1 — Establish native coverage and corroboration

On each hardware class, record kernel version, loaded EDAC modules, `mc_name`, controller count, memory type, firmware ECC setting, effective EDAC logging controls, and panic-on-UE policy. Confirm whether each `mcN` exposes all four controller counters and `seconds_since_reset`. Inventory any `dimmN` or `rankN` child, its label, location, and two DIMM counters. A blank label is allowed and must remain visibly unlabelled; do not invent a chassis slot from a sysfs ordinal.

Establish a secondary event path before calling the coverage complete. Kernel EDAC messages can provide page, syndrome, layer, and driver details not present in snapshots. The upstream rasdaemon monitors Linux kernel RAS trace events, writes to syslog/journald, and can record a persistent SQLite database when built and launched with recording support; `ras-mc-ctl` can summarize records and show sysfs error counts. Collect those sources according to local retention and privacy policy, but keep their event records out of the primary counter-delta SPL unless a separate normalization and deduplication design is tested. One physical occurrence may be represented in controller sysfs, DIMM sysfs, a trace event, a kernel line, and rasdaemon; text-line counting is not an error count.

Document unsupported paths: firmware-first APEI/GHES, x86 MCA/MCE without EDAC ownership, CXL RAS, BMC SEL, hypervisor events, and guests may require separate controls. Operate an expected-host/controller inventory and alert when the sysfs collector reports `unsupported` or `error`, when snapshots stop, or when a known controller disappears. Missing data must never be interpreted as zero errors.

## Step 2 — Deploy the read-only sysfs collector

Create a managed Universal Forwarder app named `TA_linux_edac`. Place the exact `scriptExample` body at `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA_linux_edac/bin/collect_edac.py`, owned by the deployment administrator and not writable by the forwarder service. Use the platform's approved Python 3 interpreter or a short managed launcher if `$SPLUNK_HOME/bin/python3` is not available; pin and test that launcher rather than changing the script to invoke a shell pipeline. The collector uses only Python's standard library, emits one compact JSON line per controller and exposed DIMM, and never writes sysfs.

Configure `local/inputs.conf`:

```ini
[script://$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA_linux_edac/bin/collect_edac.py]
disabled = 0
interval = 60
index = os
source = linux_edac_sysfs
sourcetype = linux:edac:sysfs
```

The index, source, source type, and app name are local conventions; change the SPL consistently if the deployment uses different names. A 60-second interval yields one controller row plus one row for each exposed DIMM/rank per poll. Keep one enabled stanza per host. Validate the winning input with `splunk btool inputs list --debug` and execute the script as the actual forwarder account. A successful run must produce stable `boot_id`, `mc`, `scope`, and `entity` identities, nonnegative integer counters, one shared observation epoch, and one controller row per `mcN`.

The script emits `unsupported` when no EDAC tree/controllers exist and `error` when a required read fails. Those health rows intentionally lack the counter contract and are excluded by the primary SPL. Create a separate source-health search for expected hosts that reports those statuses, absent controllers, duplicate host/controller/scope/entity minute buckets, poll gaps longer than two intervals plus measured ingestion allowance, malformed UUIDs, negative/noninteger values, and changing controller inventory.

## Step 3 — Parse and protect the JSON contract

Put search-time parsing in the search app or other tier where searches execute:

```ini
[linux:edac:sysfs]
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
TRUNCATE = 10000
TIME_PREFIX = "observed_at_epoch":
TIME_FORMAT = %s
MAX_TIMESTAMP_LOOKAHEAD = 10
KV_MODE = json
```

Test timestamp extraction on the installed Splunk version. If local parsing policy does not accept `%s` in this context, use an approved explicit timestamp transform and prove `_time` equals `observed_at_epoch`; do not silently use arrival time for the fixed windows. Keep each JSON object on one line. Use search-time `KV_MODE=json` only; Splunk warns that combining it with `INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=JSON` duplicates fields. Inspect the effective stanza with `btool`, preserve raw events, and restrict app changes to collection administrators.

Run a field check:

```spl
index=os source=linux_edac_sysfs sourcetype=linux:edac:sysfs earliest=-10m
| table _time host collector_status boot_id mc scope entity mc_name seconds_since_reset ce_count ue_count ce_noinfo_count ue_noinfo_count dimm_label dimm_location
```

Compare a single poll directly with the same sysfs files on that host. Controller values must match exactly. Every DIMM row must match its own `dimm_*` files; do not expect the sum of exposed DIMMs to equal the controller total because no-information events and driver granularity can differ. Confirm that each entity appears once per minute and that a restart changes `boot_id` rather than merging histories.

## Step 4 — Create and understand the reset-aware search

Save the supplied SPL as `linux_edac_memory_error_tracking`. Schedule it every five minutes on a minute boundary. The example searches from 12 minutes ago to two minutes ago, using the earlier samples as a baseline and the newest five complete minutes as the nonoverlapping alert window. The final freshness check requires a recent controller sample. Measure p95 and worst-case forwarding/indexing delay; adjust the two-minute delay, lookback, alert window, and freshness as one reviewed set. Do not simply widen the alert window, because overlapping dispatch windows can notify twice for one increment.

The first conversion and `where` clauses enforce the event schema. `stats` creates one row per minute/entity and `bucket_samples=1` rejects duplicate collectors rather than arbitrarily choosing one. Chronological `sort` is mandatory because `streamstats current=f window=1` copies the prior sample for the same host, boot, controller, scope, and entity. Partitioning by `boot_id` prevents subtraction across reboots.

For a normally increasing counter, the delta is current minus previous. If the reset timer falls or an individual counter decreases, the search marks a boundary and uses the current total as the observable post-boundary increment. That avoids a negative delta or a huge lifetime spike and still reports errors counted after the boundary. It is a lower bound: errors between the prior poll and a reset can no longer be reconstructed from sysfs. If no previous sample exists, delta is zero. This baseline rule intentionally trades first-poll sensitivity for correct attribution; kernel/rasdaemon event monitoring covers that gap.

After calculating entity deltas, the SPL sums only `scope=controller` values to determine alert count and severity. DIMM changes become strings in `changed_dimms` for localization. No-information deltas remain explicit. Any positive controller CE delta crosses the warning threshold, matching the kernel ABI's instruction to monitor nonzero CEs. Any positive controller UE delta crosses the critical threshold. There is no defensible universal vendor-independent count such as ten CEs per hour that declares a DIMM failed; rate-based escalation belongs in hardware-class policy after vendor guidance and observed baseline, while the base detection retains every new CE.

The exact exception lookup is evaluated after a real result exists. It can suppress a corrected-only notification during an approved bounded observation or injection test. The final `where` deliberately bypasses every exception when `controller_ue_delta>0`. Trigger the alert when result count is greater than zero. Throttle repeated notifications by `host,mc,alert_reason` only for the incident-management interval while preserving every scheduled result and raw snapshot.

## Step 5 — Validate semantics and collection

Run the positive and negative scenarios exactly in an isolated index with event times aligned to the saved search's complete-minute windows. Assert result values, not merely result count. Test CE and UE separately and together, no-information increments, one and multiple changed DIMMs, exact zero-to-one boundaries, a reset timer decrease with counters at zero, a reset with a positive post-reset count, a reboot with a new boot ID, duplicate buckets, a missing baseline, and stale data. Verify that the controller delta remains three when a controller and its DIMM both rise by three.

On representative nonproduction hardware, compare two successive collected snapshots with direct reads of `ce_count`, `ue_count`, both no-information counters, and `seconds_since_reset`. Compare the same interval with `journalctl -k` or the distribution's kernel log and, where deployed, rasdaemon/`ras-mc-ctl --errors`, `--summary`, or `--error-count`. Differences are diagnostic: logging may be disabled, a panic may precede polling, rasdaemon may not be recording, a source may have a different reporting owner, or a DIMM may be unlocalized. Do not force counters to change on production.

Use only vendor- and owner-approved hardware error injection on disposable or isolated test systems. Record the injection method, expected type/count/location, before/after sysfs values, kernel and rasdaemon events, Splunk raw events, alert row, host behavior, and cleanup. A synthetic Splunk fixture validates SPL but not kernel, firmware, ECC, or physical location. A real injection validates only the tested hardware/kernel path and must not be generalized to unsupported platforms.

## Step 6 — Triage and safe response

For a CE warning, preserve raw evidence, inspect the trend and recurrence by controller/DIMM, verify slot mapping against BMC/SMBIOS/vendor inventory, and correlate temperature, voltage, firmware, memory scrubbing, workload, maintenance, and recent hardware changes. Follow vendor thresholds and warranty procedures. A one-off CE is not automatically harmless and is not by itself an instruction to replace a DIMM; repeated or concentrated CEs can justify planned diagnostics or replacement.

For any UE, page the platform/hardware on-call according to service criticality. Determine whether the host panicked, isolated a page, killed a process, recovered through retry, or remained online. Preserve crash dump, pstore, kernel journal, rasdaemon database, BMC SEL, application integrity evidence, and the affected workload's state before reboot where safe. Follow the platform/vendor runbook for evacuation, memory testing, firmware review, and part replacement. Do not automatically reset counters, clear logs, reboot, offline memory, change scrubbing, or remove a DIMM from this alert; those actions can destroy evidence or worsen availability.

Build the dashboard described in `visualization`. Restrict raw hardware/error data and exception writes to appropriate operational roles. Review coverage and physical-label mapping after kernel, firmware, motherboard, memory, hypervisor, collector, Splunk, or host-identity changes. Retain events and incident evidence according to the organization's operational policy rather than an invented compliance duration.

## Step 7 — Troubleshoot product-specific failures

- **No EDAC events in Splunk:** verify the scripted input is enabled, the collector returns `ok` controller rows, the source route reaches `index=os`, and the search role can read the index. Then inspect the source-health search before changing the alert SPL.
- **No `/sys/devices/system/edac/mc`:** verify ECC-capable hardware and firmware configuration, loaded controller driver, kernel support, reporting ownership, and whether the system uses APEI/GHES, MCA/MCE, CXL, a hypervisor, or BMC-only telemetry. Do not create an empty tree or treat absence as zero.
- **`unsupported` or `error` health rows:** run the collector as the forwarder account, inspect the exact `error_path` and class, verify read/traverse permission and controller lifetime, and compare with service/kernel messages. Do not grant write access to EDAC controls.
- **Fields are null or duplicated:** inspect `_raw`, the winning `props.conf`, and the search tier. Confirm one JSON object per line, `KV_MODE=json`, and no simultaneous indexed JSON extraction.
- **Event time is wrong:** compare `_time` with `observed_at_epoch`, verify `TIME_PREFIX`, `%s` support, lookahead, timezone-independent epoch handling, and parsing-tier deployment. Wrong time breaks both baseline and nonoverlapping windows.
- **Duplicate minute buckets:** identify duplicate scripted stanzas, deployment-server layering, manual cron copies, cloned host names, or forwarding loops. The primary search rejects the bucket; fix collection rather than choosing a maximum counter.
- **Counters decrease unexpectedly:** inspect `boot_id`, `seconds_since_reset`, driver reload/rebind, writes to `reset_counters`, kernel logs, and source identity. A marked boundary is not proof of a benign reset and cannot reconstruct pre-reset events.
- **Kernel/rasdaemon reports UE but Splunk sysfs does not:** check panic-on-UE, polling timing, event ownership, driver support, rasdaemon record time, and source freshness. This is an expected blind spot in some fatal or firmware-first paths, not grounds to rewrite a log regex as a counter.
- **Controller delta rises but no DIMM changes:** inspect no-information deltas and driver granularity. Escalate with controller/page/syndrome context from kernel or rasdaemon; do not assign a slot by guess.
- **DIMM label disagrees with chassis inventory:** treat sysfs label as unverified user-space metadata, reconcile motherboard-specific mapping and serials, and correct the platform's label process before service.
- **Many old errors alert after enabling collection:** the first sample should yield zero. If it does not, verify that the search retained `current=f`, the previous-null branches, chronological ordering, and boot/controller/entity keys.
- **No alert despite a known increment:** verify a prior qualified sample, one event per minute, the complete five-minute alert window, latest-sample freshness, controller rather than DIMM-only change, and source-health exclusions. Inspect raw values before changing thresholds.
- **CIM or `tstats` has no equivalent:** expected. Keep the raw reset-aware contract or build a purpose-specific, replayable summary; do not map EDAC counters into an unrelated performance or change dataset.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the computer's own memory-error counters for new problems. If the machine had to repair a mistake we warn the team, and if it could not repair one we raise the urgency so they can protect the service and investigate the hardware.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Emit reset-aware Linux EDAC controller and DIMM counter snapshots as JSON lines."""
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/sys/devices/system/edac/mc")
BOOT_ID = Path("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id")
COLLECTOR = "linux_edac_sysfs_v1"


def text(path):
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="strict").strip()


def integer(path):
    value = int(text(path), 10)
    if value < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"negative counter: {path}")
    return value


def emit(status, observed_at_epoch, boot_id, **fields):
    event = {
        "event_version": 1,
        "collector": COLLECTOR,
        "collector_status": status,
        "observed_at_epoch": observed_at_epoch,
        "boot_id": boot_id,
    }
    event.update(fields)
    print(json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=True, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True), flush=True)


def main():
    observed = int(time.time())
    try:
        boot_id = text(BOOT_ID)
    except (OSError, UnicodeError) as exc:
        emit("error", observed, "unavailable", error_class=type(exc).__name__, error_path=str(BOOT_ID))
        return
    if not ROOT.is_dir():
        emit("unsupported", observed, boot_id, error_path=str(ROOT))
        return
    controllers = sorted(path for path in ROOT.glob("mc[0-9]*") if path.is_dir())
    if not controllers:
        emit("unsupported", observed, boot_id, error_path=str(ROOT))
        return
    for controller in controllers:
        try:
            common = {
                "mc": controller.name,
                "mc_name": text(controller / "mc_name"),
                "seconds_since_reset": integer(controller / "seconds_since_reset"),
            }
            emit(
                "ok",
                observed,
                boot_id,
                scope="controller",
                entity=controller.name,
                ce_count=integer(controller / "ce_count"),
                ue_count=integer(controller / "ue_count"),
                ce_noinfo_count=integer(controller / "ce_noinfo_count"),
                ue_noinfo_count=integer(controller / "ue_noinfo_count"),
                **common,
            )
            slots = sorted({*controller.glob("dimm[0-9]*"), *controller.glob("rank[0-9]*")})
            for slot in (path for path in slots if path.is_dir()):
                ce_path = slot / "dimm_ce_count"
                ue_path = slot / "dimm_ue_count"
                if not ce_path.is_file() or not ue_path.is_file():
                    continue
                label_path = slot / "dimm_label"
                location_path = slot / "dimm_location"
                emit(
                    "ok",
                    observed,
                    boot_id,
                    scope="dimm",
                    entity=slot.name,
                    dimm_label=text(label_path) if label_path.is_file() else "",
                    dimm_location=text(location_path) if location_path.is_file() else "",
                    ce_count=integer(ce_path),
                    ue_count=integer(ue_path),
                    **common,
                )
        except (OSError, UnicodeError, ValueError) as exc:
            emit("error", observed, boot_id, mc=controller.name, error_class=type(exc).__name__, error_path=str(controller))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
